title: Emergency retrieval & forensic access — negotiation scratchpad
content:
Purpose: quick personal notes for negotiating client requests that, during an incident or regulatory demand, ask for full live access, snapshot exports, or on-demand forensic extraction from our hosted environment. Not a final legal position — just pragmatic levers and fallback language for AE/legal to iterate on.

High-level negotiation goals:
- Protect multi-tenant isolation and secrets; avoid live access to infra/host-level.
- Offer forensically useful artifacts (timed snapshots, sanitized logs, audit trails) rather than root-level access.
- Keep obligations time-boxed (e.g., single extraction window, secure transfer method) and cost-recoverable.
- Ensure customer acknowledgement of limitations (ephemeral KV caches, missing ephemeral tokens, model nondeterminism).

Quick pocket redlines to propose (order of priority):
1) Replace "live access to production systems" with "provision of forensically-signed export package".
   - Rationale: preserves isolation and avoids escalation.
   - Suggested language: "Provider will, within X business days of a written request, deliver an encrypted forensic export package containing the artifacts listed in Appendix A. Provider will not grant remote shell or console access to customer personnel to production hosts."

2) Scope artifacts narrowly. Avoid open-ended "all data related to" phrasing.
   - Suggested artifact list: request-scoped request logs (time-bounded), model input payloads for specified request IDs, model output artifacts, audit trail for access/role changes, deployment metadata (models and versions).

3) Timeboxing and cost recovery.
   - Proposed: "Provider will complete one complimentary forensic export per 12-month period per contract; additional exports are billable at $X/hr plus fixed export fee $Y. Provider will estimate time/cost in advance and obtain Customer approval for billable work."

4) Redact/obfuscation carveouts for third-party PII / downstream data and for keys/secrets.
   - "Provider shall remove or mask any secrets, cryptographic material, and third-party personal data unless Customer provides lawful basis and indemnification for processing."

5) Chain-of-custody & signature.
   - For legal/regulatory inquiries, insist package be signed (hash + signing key) and delivered via SFTP/secure share with expiration. Include MD5/SHA256 + signer id.

6) Forensic sampling vs exhaustive export.
   - Offer sampling first: e.g., targeted IDs, time ranges, correlated request traces. If customer insists on broad export, escalate to legal + engineering and require contract amendment.

7) SLA for exports (timelines) and a limited liability cap specifically for forensic exports.
   - Suggested: "Provider uses commercially reasonable efforts to deliver export within 10 business days; liability for delays limited to re-processing fee up to $50K." (numbers placeholders).

Talking scripts / negotiation nuggets (AE/legal friendly):
- AE -> Customer: "We can provide everything that will help you forensically, but we do this by producing a time-limited, signed export so we can keep production secure. What specific IDs/time ranges are you investigating?"
- Legal -> Customer: "We can commit to a defined set of artifacts. If you need live instrumentation or broader host-level access, we need an MSA amendment and separate access controls."
- Engineering -> Customer: "To make this reproducible we need precise request IDs and time windows; otherwise we will need to do a broader search which takes more time and cost."

Edge-case clauses to flag (and proposed mitigation):
- Customer insists on "no redaction" for exported data: push for indemnity clause and explicit customer authorization for processing third-party personal data.
- Demand for "continuous" streaming of logs to customer during incident: counter with "provider will support real-time push via integration (webhook/s3) under dedicated paid subscription; otherwise we do point-in-time exports only."
- Customer wants forensic access to underlying OS or GPU memory: absolute no — escalate to SOC / execs; propose an on-site audit under strict NDA & mutual logistics if contractually essential (rare).

Sample clause alternatives (short forms):
- Customer request (bad): "Customer may access Provider production systems to perform forensic analysis upon written notice."
- Provider counter (preferred): "Customer may request a Forensic Export. Provider will produce, within [X] business days, an encrypted Forensic Export Package containing the artifacts enumerated in Appendix A. Provider will not grant shell or console access to production systems."

Appendix A (artifacts we are generally willing to produce — negotiate specifics per request):
- Request logs for specified request IDs and time window (include headers, timestamps, truncated tokens if required for PII)
- Model version and config (weights hash, quantization profile, tokenizer id)
- Inference routing metadata (region, shard id, instance class)
- Access/audit logs for relevant roles and times
- Application-level traces (span traces) correlated to request IDs
- Post-processing logs (reranking, filtering) and any function calls triggered by the request
- Note: We generally can't provide raw GPU memory dumps or host-level core dumps.

Operational checklist for intake (for AE/CS + Eng + Legal):
- 1) Request intake form (Jira ticket template): required fields: requestor name, legal basis, incident id, request IDs/time ranges, purpose, urgency, delivery method, who will receive package.
- 2) Triage meeting within 24 hours (engineering + security + legal) to scope artifacts & estimate effort.
- 3) Approve cost estimate with customer if beyond complimentary allowance.
- 4) Produce export, confirm hash, deliver via agreed channel, record chain-of-custody in ticket.
- 5) Post-delivery: run redaction pass if requested and recorded, log retention update, and create follow-up remediation tasks.

Open questions / items for legal to draft: 
- Is a flat annual complimentary export acceptable commercially, or do we need per-contract negotiation?
- Exact indemnity language when customer requests unredacted third-party data.
- Firm language to reject OS/GPU memory access while offering on-site audit alternative — need playbook for logistics/costs.
- Template Appendix A with field definitions (what is considered PII vs request metadata) — coordinate with privacy.

Notes to self / quick reminders: 
- Keep negotiation language simple for AEs to read. Provide a 1-line customer-facing summary and an internal long-form clause.
- Track these concessions centrally so we don't bleed inconsistent rights across customers. Create a short GDoc canonical template once Legal signs off.
- Engineering: build a small export toolkit (one-click forensic bundle generator) to reduce billable hours and risk of errors. Ticket: GH:pr/1234 references the prototype.

Recent precedent: customer ACME asked for console access 2024-11; we provided a signed export (4 days), charged for second export. Lessons learned: need clearer cost schedule and pre-approved CSV of fields we will redact.

Bottom-line negotiating posture (for internal use):
- Default: we provide signed export packages; no live console access; limited complimentary allowance; customer pays for scope expansion.
- Escalate to legal + VP if customer insists on host-level or continuous streaming of raw production telemetry.

End — save as canonical draft for AE cheat-sheet when Legal finalizes.
